knowledge_point.title: Determining the Critical Points of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}u \\ \left(v - 2\right)^{2} \\ w\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}\to \begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=u,\,y(u,v,w)=\left(v - 2\right)^{2},\,z(u,v,w)=w.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =1 & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2 v - 4 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =0 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 v - 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}2 v - 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)(2 v - 4\cdot(1)-(0)\cdot(0)) \\  & =2 \left(v - 2\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =0 \\ 2 \left(v - 2\right) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The critical points lie on the plane $v - 2=0.$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The critical points lie on the plane $v + 2=0.$
The critical points lie on the plane $v=0.$
The critical points lie on the plane $w - 2=0.$
The critical points lie on the plane $v - 2=0.$
The critical points lie on the plane $u - 2=0.$
